clue.text: Outstanding person repeats one element

indicators.note: repeats tells us to write the element's symbol twice in a row

parts.note: Lu is the chemical symbol for lutetium, a single element

explanation.surface: A remarkable person keeps returning to one basic point.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is informal for a remarkable or outstanding person or thing.

clue.text: Animal permitted to go outside at any time

indicators.note: to go outside says the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: A pet is allowed out whenever it likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' is vague on purpose; the wordplay pins it to a young hare.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, a particular animal.

clue.text: Girl going north on one road, then south, to find Australian fliers

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means read upwards, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Beryl is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl drives north then south looking for Australian birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' reverses BERYL to LYREB.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrebirds are Australian ground birds famed for their mimicry and lyre-shaped tails.

clue.text: Expression of disgust after upper-class Basque's drunk whisky

indicators.note: after places the exclamation behind the other pieces
drunk means the letters of the next word are reeling about into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter; the word's letters are the fodder
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone recoils as a posh Basque gets drunk on whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like it describes the Basque but is the anagram signal; 'after' places the exclamation last.
explanation.definitionFit: Usquebaugh is the Gaelic-derived old word for whisky, literally water of life.

clue.text: Train a group of swimmers

explanation.definitionFit: School as a verb means instruct, and as a noun a shoal of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Ploughed land used to tend horse

indicators.note: ploughed turns the soil over, so the following letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Farmland once ploughed was used for keeping horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughed' rearranges LAND USED.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle is to remove the saddle, a stable task in caring for a horse.

clue.text: Moreover, purchase, say, an identical voucher

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and we take its sound

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
the same token is one identical voucher

explanation.surface: Moreover, someone buys another voucher exactly like the first.
explanation.definitionFit: By the same token is an idiom meaning likewise or furthermore, adding a further point.

clue.text: Outswum all the others — that's customary

indicators.note: the others means skipping the first letter and taking every other one after it

explanation.surface: Beating all the other swimmers is just the usual thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of OUTSWUM ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and customary both describe what normally or habitually happens.

clue.text: Teacher means to make progress

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: A head teacher finds a method to advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Headway is forward movement or advancement, as in making headway with a task.

clue.text: Symbolic gesture of this Congress in dissolution

indicators.note: dissolution breaks things up, so the letters are dissolved and reformed

explanation.surface: A gesture of blessing as a congress is dissolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dissolution' rearranges OF THIS CONGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the sign of the cross is a Christian symbolic hand gesture.

clue.text: Peter out without right coat

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word surrounds the letter

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away, to vanish

explanation.surface: Something fades away for lack of the proper coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: VANISH goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a coat of glossy finish applied to wood, so the noun names a coating.

clue.text: Fruit a necessity when suffering rejection

indicators.note: rejection read as turning back, so the whole run is written backwards

parts.note: a must is a necessity
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Fruit becomes essential for someone feeling rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering rejection' turns A MUST AS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of small loose-skinned mandarin orange, a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Troublemaker below floor doing wrong

indicators.note: doing wrong suggests the letters are put out of their right order

explanation.surface: A nuisance lurking under the floorboards gets up to mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges BELOW FLOOR DOING. ROBIN GOODFELLOW is Puck, the mischievous sprite of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow, also called Puck, is the sprite of English folklore famed for mischief.

clue.text: Being frugal in most of the break

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Thrift is found in most of the gap, a financial joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is just a link here, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is the quality of careful, economical spending, the state of being sparing.

clue.text: Remove crockery, etc, omitting one area where you can't stop

indicators.note: omitting signals that a letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to clear away is to remove the dishes after a meal
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: After clearing the table, someone skips one part of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting' drops one A from CLEAR AWAY. A clearway is a British road on which stopping is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearway is a British road where vehicles are forbidden from stopping or parking.

clue.text: Nothing loth, Bill catches fish

indicators.note: catches means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: Willy, like Bill, is a pet form of William
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Bill is happy to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing loth' is an old phrase meaning not at all unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothing loth is an old phrase meaning quite willing, so the adverb describes eager readiness.

clue.text: Public money going into cost of housing — this is suggestive

indicators.note: going into says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rent is what one pays for housing
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Welfare payments go into paying the rent, which says something.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means evocative, suggestive of something, as in redolent of the past.

clue.text: Hanky-panky from the head of Military Intelligence

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, and 'of' gives the possessive MI's
a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: Something improper comes from the boss of a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of MI is MI's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief and hanky-panky both mean naughty, playful misbehaviour or trickery.

clue.text: A subscriber to omerta, Dr Keaton abandons university

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: abandons says a letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Buster Keaton was the silent-film comedian

explanation.surface: A doctor named Keaton quits university to join the Mafia.
explanation.walkthrough: Buster Keaton was the American silent-film comedian; MO (medical officer) stands for 'Dr'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Mafia's code of silence, so one bound by it is a gangster.

clue.text: Ring round clubs to find poet

parts.note: a bell is something that rings
O is round in shape
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone telephones about the clubs to track down a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal but is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer known for comic verse such as Cautionary Tales.

clue.text: Console ten for so long

parts.note: to cheer someone is to console or comfort them
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, ten

explanation.surface: Comforting a group of ten for such a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio and so long are both informal British ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Pride's damaged by small creature

indicators.note: damaged means the word's letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A lion pride is hurt by a tiny beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small creature' tempts as the definition, but 'small' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an eight-legged arachnid, a creature.

clue.text: Gap in fortification giving grounds for hope for end of engagement

parts.note: a breach is a gap made in a wall or defences
someone 'of promise' shows signs of future success

explanation.surface: A breach in the walls offers the defenders hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Breach of promise was the legal action for breaking off a promise to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Breach of promise refers to breaking a promise to marry, i.e. ending an engagement.

clue.text: Turn out to be inverted

definitions.meaning: to turn out is to finish up in some way
with the end pointing upwards, upside down

explanation.definitionFit: End up means finally become, and also describes something standing on its end, upside down.

clue.text: A little Eastern European larva

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
a Pole comes from Poland in Eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Something small from Eastern Europe in its immature stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the aquatic larva of a frog or toad.

clue.text: Doctor needs to move carefully towards river to see ship

indicators.note: towards places the letter for river after the rest

parts.note: to edge is to move cautiously little by little

explanation.surface: A doctor creeps toward the riverbank to watch a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel that scoops mud and silt from river and harbour beds.

clue.text: Methodist preacher backing one Conservative cabinet

indicators.note: backing means the preacher's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Donald Soper was a famous Methodist minister and open-air preacher
I is the Roman numeral one
Tory is the familiar name for a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Methodist minister supports a Tory member of the Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses SOPER (Lord Soper, the Methodist preacher) to REPOS. 'cabinet' poses as the government body but is a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place or receptacle where things are stored, like a cabinet.

clue.text: Literal part of party policy

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a party's policy is just a literal statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' is British printing slang for a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: In British printing jargon a literal is a misprinted letter, a slip in typesetting.
